metadata.neutral_citation: TANG PUI WAH v. YIU YAT FAN T/A DAO PONG UNITED GOODS MANUFACTORY [1985] HKCFI 68; HCA 4500/1984 (28 March 1985)
metadata.case_name: TANG PUI WAH v. YIU YAT FAN T/A DAO PONG UNITED GOODS MANUFACTORY

plaintiff.occupation_before: operating a plastic injection moulding machine

injuries.description: Removal/amputation of middle and index fingers and thumb; loss of some carpal and metercarpal bones; right hand substantially destroyed with only ring and fifth fingers present and only fourth and fifth metercarpals remaining.
source: An emergency operation was performed and the Plaintiff's middle and index fingers, his thumb and some badly damaged carpal and metercarpal bones were removed.
Dr Wedderburn described the Plaintiff's right hand as just a remnant with only the ring and fifth fingers being present. The only bones in the hand left were the fourth and fifth metercarpals.
Observation of the Plaintiff's right forearm confirms Dr Wedderburn's report. ... the hand itself was almost totally gone.
injuries.icd_description: Combined traumatic amputation of finger with other parts of wrist or hand

injuries.description: Severe crushing injury to right forearm with a dark coloured scar stretching from elbow to wrist, between 2½ and 3 inches wide, with marked muscle loss (wastage) on the back of the forearm and a deep groove along the scar.
source: As a result of the accident the Plaintiff suffered severe crushing injuries of his right hand and forearm.

Examination by Dr. Wedderburn in June of 1984 revealed a dark coloured scar stretching from the Plaintiff's elbow to his wrist on the outer aspect of the right forearm. This scar was between 2½ and 3 inches wide and there was marked muscle loss on the back of the forearm with a deep groove running down the length of the scar.
There is a deep and ugly scar from the elbow to the hand. There is clear muscle wastage ...
injuries.icd_description: Crushing injury of other specified part of forearm

manifestations.description: Extreme pain immediately following the accident and during hospital stay; continued pain after leaving hospital; pain returns during wet and damp conditions.
Can exercise a 110 lb grip with left hand but can only exercise a 5 lb grip with the right hand using ring and fifth finger (with counter-fixation).
Dark coloured scar from elbow to wrist between 2½ and 3 inches wide with marked muscle loss on back of forearm and a deep groove along the scar (plainly evident on observation).
Condition almost equivalent to an amputation at mid-hand; assessed as 54% impairment of the whole man.

treatments_received: A total of 5 operations over the next two months (including 3 skin graphs)
Physiotherapy and follow-up outpatient treatment visits
In-patient care at Princess Margaret Hospital and Caritas Hospital

losses.description: Loss of part of the right hand with removal of thumb, index and middle fingers and loss of some carpal and metacarpal bones leaving only fourth and fifth metacarpals; right hand substantially a remnant.
Deep and ugly scar from the elbow to the hand (dark coloured scar between 2½ and 3 inches wide) with marked muscle wastage and a deep groove.
Plaintiff's work options are restricted; 'this is the only type of work that is possible for him now and in the future' (he obtained work as a messenger).
